entries.title: Center Agents belong to their organizations
entries.body:
Center Agents belong to their organizations, including Personal Workspaces.
Current organization owners and admins can manage, pause, and resume them.
Removing the person who originally created the agent preserves its identity
and conversations.

Pausing a Center Agent now correctly stops its running tasks. Resuming it allows
new work without restarting cancelled tasks.

A Center Agent's Space membership no longer gives its original creator access
to a private Space. Members keep their own conversations and Space permissions.

Team lists the Center Agent first under Online instead of in a separate group.
Its card labels it as the Center Agent and names its owning organization without
adding height.

This change requires an updated CLI to read organization directories containing
Center Agents.

entries.title: Clear sent attachments from the composer immediately
entries.body:
Sending a message moves its text and attachments into the conversation immediately,
without leaving file cards or a ready-to-send count in the composer. This works
in Spaces, direct messages, and threads. Rejected messages remain recoverable,
and finishing a send does not clear attachments added to the next draft.

entries.title: Clearer message boundaries in conversations
entries.body:
Messages from other people and Agents now use a subtle neutral background,
while your own messages use a soft blue tint. The surfaces help separate
messages in busy conversations in light and dark mode, while preserving
speaker identities and your preferred message alignment.

entries.title: Easier mentions and clearer replies
entries.body:
Typing `@` after Chinese, Japanese, Korean, or sentence punctuation now opens
member suggestions without an extra space. A close button lets you dismiss
suggestions and keep your `@` and entered text as ordinary text, just like Escape.

Reply context now sits inside the composer as a compact line with the person's
name, a short message preview, and a leading cancel button. Quotes in sent
messages use quieter, single-line previews so the new reply is easier to distinguish.

Unavailable Wake targets now appear muted in the composer, with a shorter
explanation and an action to reconnect the computer or resolve the current issue.

entries.title: Edit and recall your Space messages
entries.body:
Edit your sent messages directly in the conversation, or recall them for everyone
in the Space. Clearing all content asks you to confirm recall. Recalled messages
leave a small notice, and the sender can choose Edit again to bring the last
saved version back into the composer without sending it automatically.

entries.title: Find chats and start conversations together
entries.body:
Chats now opens a searchable conversation list instead of briefly showing an empty
page and jumping into a conversation. The list follows your sidebar groups and
sorting preferences. Sidebar groups start collapsed and reveal the conversation
you open, while remembering your manual choices.

Pin chats or move them between groups directly from the list. Chats and Spaces
now offer the same search, filters, and group settings in their lists and sidebars,
including archived chat filters and Space activity filters.

New chat uses the same people-and-agents picker as Space members. Choose one person
or agent for a private chat, or choose several to create a private Space together.

entries.title: Find conversations with your Agents on your profile
entries.body:
Your profile now lists conversations involving your personal Agents, with the
people involved, recent messages, and an Agent filter. Open the existing
conversation directly without joining it just to read. The list uses the
same access rules as Chats and Spaces.

entries.title: Find your place in long conversations
entries.body:
Browse compact previews of a long Space conversation and jump directly to an
earlier message. Read nearby history, return to the latest messages, and open
pinned messages without losing your draft. Edited and recalled messages stay
current in history and pinned previews.

entries.title: Keep Agent replies working when a discussion thread opens
entries.body:
Opening a discussion thread under a running Wake no longer moves its reply away
from the original conversation or causes a false latest-message read failure.
Replies still check for newer messages before appearing.

entries.title: Keep important Space messages and files in view
entries.body:
Pin a message from its action menu to keep it above the conversation. The compact
preview shows who pinned it and lets you jump to the original message. Only the
person who pinned a message can unpin it, with no extra confirmation.

Pin files from Files to give them a separate preview above pinned messages in
the conversation. File pins open the shared file and follow its latest version.
An unread new version shows a small “New updates” badge beside the pinned filename.

entries.title: Keep long message previews complete
entries.body:
Long messages now fold around 2,000 characters, finishing complete paragraphs
and Markdown blocks instead of cutting through words, lists, tables, or code.
A subtle fade marks the folded edge. Show more expands the original message
in place in Spaces, chats, and threads.

entries.title: Keep pending Agent actions within reach
entries.body:
Agent owners can handle pending permissions, questions, and plan reviews from a
quiet action surface above the currently visible Space or Thread composer, so
required input no longer gets buried in message history or behind an open Thread.

The action strip now sits against the composer and expands into a consistent
card for plans, questions, and permissions. Long details scroll within the card,
with subtle edge fades and response buttons that stay within reach.

entries.title: Make Stop easier to spot
entries.body:
Stop now has a subtle background and border beside the working Agent message,
making it easier to recognize as a button without using a warning color.

entries.title: React to Space messages
entries.body:
Add emoji reactions to messages and thread replies, click again to remove your
reaction, and view who reacted. Reactions stay with the message and are included
when agents read Space messages and history, without sending a new message or
waking an agent.

entries.title: Recognizable names for new Codex sessions
entries.body:
New Codex sessions started by a Wake get a short name based on the Agent and
request, making them easier to find. Naming runs while the Agent works and does
not hold up the task if it fails. Existing session names stay unchanged.

entries.title: Keep Agent creation open from the Space members drawer
entries.body:
On smaller screens, creating or selecting an Agent from Space members no longer
closes the picker when you click inside it. The members drawer and its dialogs
share focus and dismissal handling, while preserving swipe-to-close behavior.

entries.title: Keep Agent creation trackable when setup takes longer
entries.body:
Agent creation now returns a trackable request while setup continues on the
server. A lost response can recover the same request, and an uncertain result
no longer tells you that creation failed. Repeating the same intent preserves
the original Agent, including when its remaining setup needs attention.

entries.title: Choose Space recipients independently of message text
entries.body:
Space messages no longer interpret `@Name(wake)` or similar text as an action.
Choose a recipient in the Web or terminal picker, or pass a full Profile ID with
`--wake`, `--reference`, or `--mention` in the CLI. Names containing parentheses
remain readable without changing who receives the message.

Pasting ordinary member names also keeps them as plain text. Copying an existing
OpenMeld mention preserves its selected recipient and relation.

Update scripts that embed recipient instructions in message text to use the
explicit flags. The optional `--plain` flag asserts that no recipients were
provided. Existing messages and already-dispatched Wakes retain their identity
and delivery records.

entries.title: Invite teammates with fewer steps
entries.body:
Open Invite people from your avatar menu to send an email invitation or share a
link. The same controls appear first in Invitations settings, with empty review
and acceptance lists hidden.

Links created by owners and admins let verified recipients join directly.
Ordinary members can request invitations; every owner and admin receives an urgent
Inbox item and review email, and one approval is enough. People who request to
join through a link can enter after approval without accepting a second invitation.
Setup now shows the correct Join or Request to join action. New links expire after
30 days; existing request links continue to require approval.

entries.title: Keep Slack mentions connected to shared context
entries.body:
Slack mentions recover message text, attachment details, and referenced messages
from the same channel, including replies in threads. Working status appears
before these lookups. When Slack cannot provide part of that context, the
Center Agent receives a clear limitation instead of treating the context as
complete.

entries.title: Retire the separate Center Agent Task workspace
entries.body:
Center Agent work continues in chat sessions. The separate Task board, Task
pages, creation and query tools, APIs, and Task Inbox updates are removed.
Local Agent execution handles, stopping, waiting, and result callbacks remain
available. Existing chat messages remain readable.

entries.title: Clearer computer connection guidance
entries.body:
Computer setup shows short instructions for copying the command, opening Terminal,
and following the prompts. Connected computers have a direct management link,
while the standalone connection page remains available for adding a computer.
Center Agent chat offers management before starting another connection flow.

Create a Space and Show me around now add a suggestion to the composer without
replacing your draft or sending a message. You decide when to send. The computer
setup panel also has a close button and follows the surrounding card layout.

Computer Connection keeps automatic updates in its options menu and hides the
setting when its value cannot be read. Agent creation lists computers rather than
their historical connections; a single computer does not require a computer choice.
Technical connection selection remains available in advanced details when needed.

Optional computer details that fail to upload no longer undo a successful
registration. Registration alone still does not mean an Agent is ready to run.

entries.title: Clearer computer status and precise computer controls
entries.body:
Computer status distinguishes a live connection, a normal disconnection, and a
status that could not be checked. Saved computer records no longer count as proof
that a local agent can run.

Computer settings and CLI diagnostics target the selected computer and
environment. The Center Agent looks up the requesting teammate's local agents
instead of assuming the Organization owner's computer is the target.

CLI integrations must update for the new `computer list --view agent` payload:
`computers` includes explicit connection evidence and `isThisComputer` identifies
the local installation. This replaces the old routing-preference interpretation.

entries.title: Keep existing chats writable after the preview upgrade
entries.body:
Existing chats now create the message preview counter during their database
upgrade. Sending a message no longer fails because the chat already completed
an earlier database version. Existing messages and preview ordering are preserved.

entries.title: More reliable command reconnection and directory reads
entries.body:
Center Agent can detach from a command while its output connection is still
opening without trying to open that connection twice. Detaching does not stop
or restart the command.

Large organization directories can be read in bounded pages, preserving member
and Agent details with explicit totals and continuation cursors. The Agent must
finish the pages before treating a roster or identity match as complete.

entries.title: Retire completed Remote Agent rollout fallbacks
entries.body:
Remote Agent now requires the current Core contracts for Slack results,
Message Channel account linking, and connected App progress. It no longer
downgrades requests or progress metadata for older Core versions. Keep Core
current before deploying this worker; roll back Remote Agent first when
reverting those Core contracts. Existing local clients and saved conversation
formats are unchanged.

entries.title: Connect Cloudflare R2 with an API token
entries.body:
Connect Cloudflare R2 using an API token and account ID from its Plugin page.
The token option is available for both personal and organization access.

entries.title: Connect Slack with Agent status support
entries.body:
Connecting Slack now requests the permission needed to show the Center Agent's
working status in threads. Existing Slack apps can enable the Agent experience
and grant the added permission without creating a replacement app.

entries.title: Distinguish confirmation requests from completed actions
entries.body:
Center Agent work summaries identify actions that are waiting for confirmation
instead of describing them as already executed. Confirmation requests remain
separate from completed actions when similar steps are grouped together.

entries.title: Stop Center Agent commands and continue chatting
entries.body:
Stopping a Center Agent request now stops its long-running Computer commands
without stopping commands from another chat. The stopped outcome replaces
temporary progress or failure messages, and you can continue the conversation
afterward.

Temporary callback failures retry until the outcome can be delivered. Stopped
requests remain available in diagnostics instead of appearing to be missing.

When a Computer runtime is replaced, the Agent receives an explicit command
loss and can inspect saved files before continuing. Lost commands are not
silently relaunched, and cleanup does not turn recovered work into a failure.

entries.title: Update your Center Agent while it works
entries.body:
Send a text update in your Center Agent chat while it is working to add a
correction or missing detail to that response. Updates stay attached to the
original response, including during network retries. If an update cannot be
confirmed before the response ends, the chat tells you so you can review the
result and send it again.

entries.title: Work in separate Center Agent chats
entries.body:
Use New chat to start a separate conversation with your Center Agent, then
switch between conversations from Chats. Each chat keeps its own history,
draft, and files view, so you can work on several requests at once without
combining their conversation context. The chats share your Center Agent's
cloud Computer.

entries.title: Check Space members without leaving the conversation
entries.body:
Space member names now open a compact profile card with useful, local context:
people show when they were last active in that Space, ordinary Agents link to
their proper editor, and Center Agent chat opens Home instead of a Direct
Message.

entries.title: Clarify Space activity times and historical profiles
entries.body:
Space member lists and profile popovers now say "Here 2d ago" to distinguish
activity in that Space from activity elsewhere in the app. Live status is
unchanged.

Profiles opened from older messages stay compact when current member details
are unavailable, without falling back to a table of technical IDs or implying
an online status.

entries.title: Clearer Agent progress and response feedback
entries.body:
Agent progress uses consistent status orbs for connecting, waiting, working,
replying, and requests that need your response. Space sidebar indicators give
requests needing your input priority over ongoing work.

Progress stays next to the message, above its actions. Pending requests remain
above the Composer, and sending a response no longer implies that the Agent
has already resumed. Plan reviews render formatted Markdown.

entries.title: Clearer computer status and setup retries
entries.body:
Disconnected computers no longer make every local Agent look broken. Agent
cards show when the computer is disconnected or its status is being checked,
while preserving your saved on/off settings.

Canceling an account switch leaves the existing computer account unchanged and
updates the setup page. If computer authorization fails, the CLI explains how
to get a new command, and Web offers a fresh attempt without a page reload.

entries.title: Find new models when configuring local Agents
entries.body:
Local Agent model selectors show a small New badge beside newly added options,
including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and supported Cursor and OpenCode models.
The badge also appears on the selected model when creating or editing a Profile.

Codex keeps GPT-5.6 Sol with High reasoning as its new-Profile recommendation.
Claude recommends Opus 5 with model-default reasoning. Existing explicit model
selections and remembered creation preferences are preserved; Claude Profiles
that rely on the runtime default use Opus 5 instead of Opus 4.8.

entries.title: Give Agent creation its own page and reduce status reads
entries.body:
Create Agent now opens its own page without the Agent-list sidebar. Existing
creation links redirect there, and creating an Agent opens its details.

Agent requests now loads sidebar status instead of leaving every Agent on
Checking. Organization status reads also avoid repeated Runtime and Controller
lookups within the same request, while each new request still reads fresh facts.

entries.title: Invite someone directly into a Space
entries.body:
Organization owners and admins can invite someone by email from a Space.
Recipients review the invitation, join the organization if needed, and land
directly in that Space. Pending invitations can be reviewed, resent, or
revoked, with matching commands for local agents using the CLI.

The member picker also checks an Agent's owner when that person will join with
the selected Agent, so the selection matches who is actually being added.

entries.title: Keep Agent status updates focused
entries.body:
Agent availability refreshes now stay on the affected Agent, keep names and
stable status labels still, and point missing working folders to one clear
recovery action. Computers also keep an available OpenMeld Tools update visible
when a local agent needs sign-in.

entries.title: Keep diagnostic records for Web application errors
entries.body:
Web application errors now produce searchable Cloudflare logs with build
identifiers, error categories, and code locations. Browser reports omit private
page content and credentials. Hosted Web releases retain private browser source
maps to help operators investigate errors after an update.

entries.title: Keep OpenMeld Tools status clear
entries.body:
The OpenMeld Tools status no longer displays a local agent's logo. Each agent's
readiness and sign-in status remain in the Local agents section.

entries.title: Keep the OpenMeld guide current without another CLI upgrade
entries.body:
OpenMeld can maintain its local Agent guide independently of the CLI, keeping
the last working copy when a download or installation fails. Before a local
task, Service checks the selected Agent's guide and supplies a public reading
link when the installed copy is unavailable.

The public guide starts with a short entry and loads detailed topics only as
needed. New instructions are installed only when the local CLI supports them.
Existing installations need the bridge CLI/Service update once to enable this
maintenance path.

entries.title: Link directly to Space messages
entries.body:
Space members can copy a direct message or thread-message link from Message
Details without adding another inline message action. Local agents can build
the same destination through the CLI and carry it through the shared Space
access check.

entries.title: More accurate activity times and reliable Space reading positions
entries.body:
People shows a person's latest activity across the app, while each Space shows
their latest visit or message there. Background reconnections no longer make
someone appear recently active, and elapsed times stay current.

Returning to a Space restores the message you were reading instead of jumping
to the bottom, including when earlier history or images finish loading.

entries.title: Open Spaces and messages without waiting on identity
entries.body:
Returning to a Space now restores its recent conversation and exact reading
position sooner. Member controls, profile details, Direct Message avatars, and
People connection states also remain useful and honest while current data is
still loading, and repeated Space image previews reuse the same downloaded
content.

entries.title: Prepare model updates for review automatically
entries.body:
A twice-daily collector prepares model-update pull requests with official source
evidence and clear decisions for the reviewing coding agent. Confirmed Codex
catalog additions are prepared automatically; account access and product defaults
remain explicit review decisions.

New Agent Profile recommendations can be configured independently of runtime
defaults, while preserving existing selections and remembered preferences.

entries.title: Preserve page loading errors during refresh
entries.body:
When an older page cannot load a component after an update, automatic refresh
preserves the original loading error instead of replacing it with a misleading
missing-component error while the refresh is pending.

entries.title: See clear Wake progress everywhere
entries.body:
Space, CLI, and the Center Agent now present the same authoritative Wake state.
Space distinguishes a sent request, a real queue, runtime connection, active
work, reply writing, posting, retries, and required Human input instead of
folding them into one generic working label. Live state changes refresh the Web
conversation immediately, while reconnect and low-frequency recovery checks
keep the view accurate after a browser sleeps or misses an update.

Members and agents can also inspect who requested the Wake, its public
source-message preview and thread, the working Agent, and the current phase.

entries.title: Start a new Wake from the composer
entries.body:
Historical Wake failures no longer offer a shortcut that reruns the original
request. To run it again, send a new message from the Space composer. Message
details still provides diagnostics and recovery for an existing result when
available. The Center Agent no longer exposes the retired execution-retry tool.

entries.title: Verify OpenMeld Service updates before reporting success
entries.body:
OpenMeld 0.3.156 is the first release with both automatic update delivery and
verified Service startup. Version 0.3.155 can update automatically; version
0.3.153 needs one manual `openmeld upgrade --yes` bridge to reach this reliable
baseline. Background updates now wait for a positive safe-switch signal, keep
running Agent work intact, report restored updates as failures, and avoid
asking users to repair a healthy Service while macOS is still starting it.

entries.title: Create and understand Agents without misleading gaps
entries.body:
New Agents now appear immediately at the top of their owner's list and show an
honest checking state while Wake availability loads, without briefly claiming
the Agent does not exist or cannot be reached. The local Agent picker also keeps
the user's latest choice instead of snapping back to an earlier selection.
Teammates can see the same safe Agent identity, avatar, public setup, and compact
activity summary whether the Agent is available, checking, or offline, while
private computer and local execution details remain owner-only.

entries.title: Recover stuck OpenMeld Service upgrades
entries.body:
OpenMeld setup now recovers when an older Service is stuck closing a stale
connection, while preserving active local work and durable results. Computer
details also distinguish a delayed local-agent check from a disconnected
Service, show when the last trusted check completed, and offer a focused retry.

entries.title: Add the current Agent to a Space without profile scans
entries.body:
`openmeld space add-me` now creates a fresh Agent Profile by default instead of
scanning every existing profile and Binding. Agents can reuse one remembered
Profile by passing its exact ID, including continuing that same Profile after a
partially completed attempt instead of creating a duplicate. New Profile
creation now returns a compact recovery receipt before later setup work, profile
creation rejects session options it cannot honor, and routine Agent View profile
output keeps diagnostics behind `--details` so the requested facts stay easy to
find.

entries.title: See OpenCode provider capacity before starting work
entries.body:
OpenCode now shows provider-by-provider capacity on Computers. OpenCode Go
reports its 5-hour, weekly, and monthly limits, and OpenMeld checks the selected
provider's supported limits before starting new work without letting another
provider's capacity block the Agent Profile.

entries.title: Keep one OpenMeld Tools update in control
entries.body:
OpenMeld Tools updates now join an update already in progress instead of
starting a competing CLI or Setup path. Manual Setup waits and continues
automatically. On the Computer page, the button stays disabled with an active
`Updating…` cue after a refresh, and the concise status moves through
`Checking…`, `Finishing…`, `Updating…`, or `Verifying…`.

Automatic updates can also respond to a newly available release over the
Service's existing connection when that Service explicitly supports the
request. Update actions bypass an older version cached by the running Service,
while simultaneous checks still share one fresh request. Startup, reconnect,
and hourly checks remain as fallbacks, failed connections can retry promptly,
and active Agent work still finishes before OpenMeld switches the Service
version.

The CLI update prompt now also restarts a newly installed standalone binary
without treating its internal build path as a command, so the menu continues
cleanly after the upgrade.

Update cleanup is also isolated to the current OpenMeld lane, so a Development
or Canary Service cannot block or be stopped by a Production update. After a
repair reaches the requested version, the Computer page now shows the current
healthy result instead of keeping a historical update failure on screen.

entries.title: Find people and their computers together
entries.body:
People now keeps Human Profiles in a dedicated sidebar and opens each person's
full details in the main view. Computer cards live with their owner, invitations
share one dialog, and the current Computer is always one click away from the
bottom toolbar. Computer status now follows the current OpenMeld Service
connection, so a registered Computer never looks ready only because OpenMeld
has seen it before.

The People sidebar now groups teammates as **Connected** or **Not Connected**
based on whether they have connected a Computer, with plain-language tooltips
for both labels. Your own profile stays first, while teammates in each group are
ordered by when they were last seen in OpenMeld Web. Activity uses compact copy
such as **3 hours ago**, explains **Last seen 3 hours ago** on hover, and sits on
the same row as Local Agent icons. Empty Channel rows no longer reserve space.
Opening or returning to OpenMeld Web now refreshes your last-seen time; using the
CLI alone does not.

entries.title: Keep Computer details honest while they refresh
entries.body:
Opening a teammate's Computer now waits for a fresh Organization Computer
projection before deciding that the Computer no longer exists, so an older
cached list cannot briefly hide required update guidance.

entries.title: Keep pending Service updates on the newest version
entries.body:
When a newer OpenMeld Service version becomes available while an update is
already waiting, OpenMeld now replaces the older target with the newer version.
The existing update remains recoverable until the newer target is safely saved,
and an older worker or queued request cannot overwrite that target or move the
Service back to an earlier version.

entries.title: Keep Space conversations comfortably centered
entries.body:
Space conversations now stay comfortably centered on wide screens while still
adapting to smaller windows, so messages remain easier to follow without
stretching across the page.

entries.title: Manage Agents in one focused workspace
entries.body:
Agents now uses the same focused sidebar-and-detail layout as People. Browse
Agents by owner, review their real Wake availability, handle Agent requests,
open a Direct Message, and edit an Agent in place without losing your current
selection. Search by name, owner, Controller, or model, and scan compact Agent
icons that stay visually aligned with People avatars.

entries.title: See how a Space can be found and opened
entries.body:
OpenMeld CLI now separates Organization visibility from link access in Space
lists and status output. An invite-only Space is no longer mistaken for
members-only when anyone with its link can open it.

entries.title: Show when a local agent is truly unavailable
entries.body:
Local agents that are signed out or blocked by provider access now appear as
Unavailable instead of a red launch error. Computers and Agent Profiles use the
newest exact local runtime evidence, distinguish temporary rate limits from
hard account or quota blockers, and point to the provider action needed before
the agent can run again.

entries.title: Edit Agent settings without leaving active work
entries.body:
Agent owners can save model, reasoning, and permission settings while a Wake is
running, including from an in-Space permission request. A Permission Mode
change can now reach later tool requests in that running session when the local
agent supports a native live update. Requests that were already waiting still
need their own response, and unsupported agents keep the mode they started
with. OpenCode permissions remain saved for new work, while disruptive
Controller changes, unbinding, and working-folder changes stay unavailable
until active work finishes.

entries.title: Connect computers without waiting for Agent setup
entries.body:
Connecting a computer now finishes as soon as its OpenMeld Service is safely
running. Local Agents continue preparing in the background, setup commands stay
fresh while the Connect page is open, and OpenMeld automatically recovers more
stale Service installations without asking the user to diagnose them.

entries.title: Let Center Agent choose the right tools
entries.body:
Center Agent now searches its complete capability catalog itself instead of
having OpenMeld guess a few tools from the wording of each request. The same
approach works across supported models, languages, and paraphrases. A small set
of safe member and Task reads stays ready for immediate use, while writes remain
under the Agent's explicit choice and current-status questions distinguish a
fresh read from older Task history. If a model provider completes a turn with
no answer or action at all, OpenMeld now safely retries once before showing a
failure.

entries.title: Setup now reports the final Service state safely
entries.body:
Computer setup now finishes successfully after OpenMeld Service recovers from
a temporary start delay, and shows the Service as connected even when no local
agents are installed yet. Development, Staging, and Canary setup also stay
isolated from the published OpenMeld Service on the same computer.

entries.title: Setup recovers from interrupted downloads
entries.body:
Computer setup now retries a temporarily interrupted OpenMeld download inside
the same command, instead of making the user copy and run the setup command
again.

entries.title: GLM 5.3 Flash is the new Center Agent default
entries.body:
The Center Agent now runs new turns on GLM 5.3 Flash instead of Grok 4.6.
Organizations that did not pick a specific model follow the default on their
next turn; organizations that explicitly selected a model keep that exact
model, and Grok 4.6 stays selectable.

Center Agent settings now also describes the image path accurately: images use
the dedicated vision model before the selected primary model receives the
description.

OpenCode Agent Profiles also gain the current curated OpenCode Go, free-tier,
and Zen model lineup, including GLM 5.3 Flash on OpenCode Go, with each
model's official reasoning variants.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent actions relevant
entries.body:
Center Agent replies no longer show an unrelated Computer setup, Space, or
Project button merely because the agent checked one of those resources while
working. An action appears only when opening that destination is the useful
next step for the current request.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent requests moving through Computer reconnects
entries.body:
Center Agent requests now recover when the private Computer reconnects while a
turn is being prepared. OpenMeld resumes the same request from durable state
before any model or tool work starts, without repeating completed external
actions. If recovery cannot finish, the request reaches one clear failure
instead of remaining indefinitely active.

entries.title: Read Organization members and Tasks with the Center Agent
entries.body:
The Center Agent can page through Organization members without loading
unrelated Agent Profile readiness, and can read the requester's canonical
OpenMeld Tasks separately from local coding-agent task handles.

entries.title: Stop waiting when Center Agent work has failed
entries.body:
When Center Agent work ends in failure, OpenMeld now reports that same final
outcome in the conversation, progress checks, diagnostics, and the CLI Wake
trace summary. Agents no longer keep waiting, treat a failed turn as an
ordinary reply, or suggest that a failed response is still being published.

entries.title: Keep browser notification setup out of the way
entries.body:
Browser notification setup now disappears completely after permission is
granted, “Not now” is selected, or the new close button is used, so members can
immediately continue setup or use the page underneath it.

entries.title: Keep Center Agent completion times accurate
entries.body:
Center Agent diagnostics now keep the time a task first completed when a final
confirmation is safely replayed. Repeated confirmations no longer make a
completed task look slower than it was.

entries.title: Let Agents reply without a shell approval prompt
entries.body:
Agents can now choose and record a Space reply, final status, or silent outcome
through a dispatch-scoped OpenMeld tool without asking the member to approve an
OpenMeld shell command. This does not relax the Agent Profile's normal Codex
permissions. Multi-paragraph replies also preserve real line breaks, literal
`\n` text, quotes, backslashes, emoji, and shell-like characters without
rewriting the message. The dispatch-scoped CLI remains available as a fallback
and for replies with attachments.

entries.title: Prevent incompatible Local Agent model choices
entries.body:
When a selected Local Agent installation clearly cannot run a model, OpenMeld
now disables that model while an Agent Profile is created or edited. The dialog
explains why and links directly to the Computer where the member can update or
change the installation. Missing compatibility information does not block the
member or make OpenMeld guess. Existing Agents that hit the same problem during
a Wake now get the same direct Computer recovery path.

entries.title: Send and safely retry Center Agent Slack messages
entries.body:
Center Agent can send formatted Slack messages again and retry the same message
when OpenMeld fails while preparing it, before anything reaches Slack.
Genuinely uncertain Slack delivery outcomes remain safely blocked so a retry
cannot create a duplicate.

entries.title: Get browser alerts for important Inbox updates
entries.body:
Members can enable browser notifications for directly addressed messages,
actions, urgent items, and requested work endings. OpenMeld avoids interrupting
the conversation already on screen, checks the latest Inbox state before a
queued alert appears, and keeps failed deliveries retryable across account or
conversation changes, refreshes, busy Inbox pages, and multiple tabs.

entries.title: Keep Codex update guidance tied to its installation
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer compares the Codex included with the ChatGPT app against the
standalone Codex CLI release. ChatGPT app installations stay under the app's
own update channel, while npm and Homebrew installations continue to use their
matching package channels. Codex usage details also put the overall weekly
limit first and use a lighter circular gauge.

entries.title: Keep disabled local agents out of the way
entries.body:
Local agents that you turn off now stay visually quiet and no longer create a
Computer alert. Installation choices also sit with the local agent's launch
details, and OpenMeld waits for the final result before calling a slow setting
change a failure.

entries.title: Recover transient local sign-in reads
entries.body:
OpenMeld now retries one temporarily unavailable saved sign-in read before it
blocks a command, so a brief local credential-store failure does not
unnecessarily stop Space file work. If the saved sign-in remains unavailable,
OpenMeld keeps the diagnostic reason and sanitized lower-level cause in Agent
View and `--json`, then asks the caller to retry or inspect authentication
status instead of incorrectly claiming that the sign-in is invalid. Unexpected
credential-read exceptions follow the same unavailable path instead of being
silently treated as a missing session. Expired, revoked, mismatched, and
genuinely invalid sessions still fail closed.

entries.title: See which local agent installation OpenMeld uses
entries.body:
Computer details now name the exact local agent installation OpenMeld uses and
show provider limits in compact circular cards. Choosing another installation
requires confirmation, stays readable on smaller screens, and no longer shows
a timeout when the computer completed the change.

entries.title: Keep Codex permissions stable during background checks
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer changes a Codex conversation's approval or sandbox settings
while checking it in the background or recovering an interrupted task. Your
selected Agent Controller Permission Mode now remains in effect for later work.

entries.title: Recover a Mac with a fresh setup command
entries.body:
Fresh setup commands on supported Macs now use the normal macOS Keychain
without requiring a restricted app entitlement. If Keychain is temporarily
unavailable or does not answer within five seconds, OpenMeld stops waiting,
clearly warns the user, keeps the session in private local storage, and finishes
reconnecting the computer. It does not keep retrying Keychain in the same
process. A later successful setup or login automatically moves the session back
to Keychain. OpenMeld Service also reuses its loaded session instead of
repeatedly querying secure storage while it is running.

entries.title: Stop background Keychain authorization windows
entries.body:
OpenMeld no longer opens macOS Keychain password dialogs while local agents are
working in the background or while setup is recovering the computer. Normal
Keychain access stays silent. If macOS requires approval, OpenMeld stops the
Keychain operation immediately, uses its protected local fallback during setup,
and leaves no waiting helper or orphaned password window behind. Developer and
npm CLI paths also stop immediately instead of launching macOS's interactive
`security` tool, so parallel local work cannot queue repeated password dialogs.

entries.title: Collapse sidebar groups when you need more room
entries.body:
The main sidebar now groups People, Agents, and Computers under Team and lets
you collapse Work, Team, and Resources. OpenMeld remembers those choices as you
move between pages, while compact sidebars keep every destination available.

entries.title: Help the Center Agent find the right capability
entries.body:
The Center Agent now loads a small set of tools relevant to each request and
searches the same organized catalog before treating a hidden tool as missing.
This also lets a verified member ask from any current Slack conversation to
privately invite named teammates, while exact directory matching and Core
authorization keep every invitation scoped to the requested people.

entries.title: More reliable Slack onboarding
entries.body:
OpenMeld now keeps Slack setup and welcome delivery recoverable, avoids sending
the same welcome twice, respects the Organization's working language, and only
lets a verified member invite exact Slack teammates through Core-bound private
delivery.

entries.title: Open exact Slack messages from Inbox
entries.body:
Inbox now links Center Agent Slack updates to the exact Slack message. Opening
the link marks the OpenMeld item read, and temporary Slack permalink failures
are retried without creating duplicate Inbox items. Existing Slack items are
upgraded in place without resetting their read, action, or dismissal state.
Tabs left open during the rollout keep the prior Center Agent destination until
they reload the current Web client.

entries.title: Publish only to verified Slack threads
entries.body:
Center Agent thread replies now require an exact Slack message link from the
request or the Slack evidence it just read. OpenMeld verifies that link against
the connected workspace before publishing, so an invented channel or timestamp
cannot redirect the reply.

entries.title: Review and save Profile Report updates
entries.body:
Pending Profile Report updates now explain that they need to be reviewed and
saved. The existing **Save changes** action accepts the visible update even when
no text edit is needed, then clears the matching Inbox action.

entries.title: See computers and connected accounts in People
entries.body:
Human Profile cards now show clear Computer status, existing Profile Reports,
and connected Slack, Lark, or Feishu accounts without exposing internal profile
handles or vague activity labels. Members can complete missing setup from their
own card, disconnect a wrong account, and securely move a provider account to
the right OpenMeld profile after proving control in that channel.

entries.title: See the same Computer status everywhere
entries.body:
Computer cards, detail pages, and navigation now use the same status and
attention color. An available update stays amber everywhere, while required
repairs stay red and Computer details keep one clear OpenMeld Service action.

entries.title: Understand every organization computer
entries.body:
The Home directory now includes every computer shared with the Organization,
even when it has no Agent Profile. Members can also ask the Center Agent or
their own local agent about computers: the Center Agent receives model-safe
owner diagnostics only in the member's private conversation, local agents can
read the authenticated user's complete CLI inventory, and teammate lookups stay
limited to the same safe summary shown in the Organization directory.

entries.title: Use the current Service's controls
entries.body:
Computer controls now follow the newest OpenMeld Service session for that
device and lane. An older reconnecting session can no longer make file access,
folder selection, Project controls, or local Agent controls appear available
when the current Service does not support them.

entries.title: A shared Changelog workflow for coding agents
entries.body:
OpenMeld contributors can record, validate, publish, and historically backfill
product changes through one Git-backed workflow that works across coding
agents.

entries.title: Ask the Center Agent what changed in OpenMeld
entries.body:
Organization members can ask the Center Agent what is new in OpenMeld and get
an answer grounded in the official published Changelog across Web, Slack, and
other supported Channels.

entries.title: Read official OpenMeld updates on the Web
entries.body:
Anyone can read the official OpenMeld Changelog at a public Web page, with
clear publication dates, release names, product areas, and older-update
pagination backed by the same GitHub record used by the Center Agent.
